summary: This bill amends the Federal Power Act to bar multi-state transmission providers from allocating costs of any facility built to carry out one state's energy policy to consumers in another state unless that state expressly consents.

scores.thoughts: The bill amends the Federal Power Act to regulate cost allocation for interstate transmission facilities among utility consumers. It does not involve any federal appropriations, government budgets, or public expenditures.
No provisions address taxes, tax rates, deductions, or revenue collection.
The legislation concerns electric transmission rates and has no connection to healthcare policy or systems.
No relation to firearms, regulations, or Second Amendment issues.
Unrelated to immigration, borders, or related protections.
No provisions touching on reproductive rights or abortion access.
Does not affect military budgets, defense procurement, or armed forces policy.

The bill regulates cost allocation for transmission facilities built to implement state policies (which could include renewable energy mandates). However, it does not create, expand, or limit any environmental regulations or protections; it is strictly a ratemaking and cost-causation measure under the Federal Power Act.
No impact on welfare programs, entitlements, or social assistance.
Completely unrelated to schools, education funding, or school choice.
No connection to drug enforcement, decriminalization, or controlled substances.
Does not address sentencing, policing, or justice system reforms.
Unrelated to tariffs, trade agreements, or globalization.
No provisions concerning deficits, debt reduction, or fiscal policy.
No bearing on LGBTQ legal protections or rights.
Does not involve foreign assistance or international aid.
Unrelated to voting access, election integrity, or electoral processes.
No provisions on technology regulation, data privacy, or digital oversight.
Does not address worker protections, union rights, or employment relations.
No engagement with religious exemptions or anti-discrimination rules.
